sections.title: What Levi's Projects is
sections.body:
Levi's Projects is a goal system with an AI teammate called **Wingman**. You capture work by speaking or typing, Wingman structures it and drafts what it can, and you approve everything before it leaves your hands.

The purpose, stated plainly: **leverage AI to accomplish your goals, faster and better.**

The five destinations in the left nav:
- **Today** — your brief, today's focus, and how the crew is loaded.
- **Missions** — the project board: Backlog, In progress, Top 3, Needs review, Done.
- **Goals** — the outcomes work is supposed to move.
- **Crew** — who is on the team and what they are carrying.
- **Wingman** — its queue, its memory, and the plays it can run.

**Needs review** appears in the nav on its own the moment Wingman has something waiting for you, with an amber count. It is the surface where delegated work comes back.

What Wingman will not do, by design: it does not operate other systems for you, it does not buy anything, and it never sends or completes anything without you pressing the button.

sections.title: Your first day
sections.body:
1. Tap **＋ New task** or the mic and describe something real: *"Get the investor update out this week — pull the numbers, draft the email, I review before it sends."*
2. Wingman structures it and shows a preview. It also asks about anything it could not work out — a due date, what done looks like, whether there is something it should read first. Answer what you know and skip the rest.
3. Choose **Do-it** (Wingman drafts) or **Track-it** (you do it, this just tracks it).
4. Confirm. If Wingman is drafting, the card lands in **Needs review** when it is ready.
5. Open the draft, refine it with an instruction, approve it.

If you pick Do-it but never say what done looks like, the card parks in **Waiting** on you rather than being drafted against a guess. Tell it the target and it will pick the work up.

sections.title: Capture a task (speak or type)
sections.body:
**Speak:** tap the amber mic — in the sidebar, or the round mic on the phone bar — talk normally, then Continue.
**Type:** tap **＋ New task**; the box is focused and the mic stays off.

Either way Wingman reads the whole sentence for a title, a workspace, a due date ("Friday", "next week"), an owner if you name one, and what the task **produces**.

Then it asks about the gaps. The questions are worked out from what it actually missed, so it will never ask when something is due if you already said Friday. One question carries a **MATTERS MOST** marker: *what does done look like?* That answer is what Wingman drafts against, and a task without one produces vague work.

Multi-step requests get split into parts, each with its own owner chip you can tap to reassign.

sections.title: What a task produces
sections.body:
Every card has a **Produces** type. Wingman guesses it from the task and marks the guess with a **GUESS** chip — tap it once to confirm, and it becomes **CONFIRMED**. A guess nobody confirms stays a guess.

The types: Document, Spreadsheet, Deck, Image, Email, Research, Plan, Decision, Call, Purchase, Setup, Review, Admin, Learning, Other.

**Setup** is configuration work inside somebody else's system — onboarding, dashboards, provisioning. **Review** is judging work someone else did. **Admin** is access, accounts, forms and subscriptions. **Learning** is training and courses.

If the type is wrong, change it in the dropdown on the task detail. Recurring upkeep — habits and chores — deliberately has no type, because it does not produce anything.

sections.title: Real files, not just text
sections.body:
When a task produces a **Document** or a **Spreadsheet** and Wingman has drafted it, a **▸ Build the docx** (or xlsx) button appears next to the type on the task detail. Pressing it turns the draft into a real Office file and attaches it to the card, where the existing download control can reach it.

A spreadsheet needs a table in the draft. If there is no table, Wingman refuses rather than handing you a one-column sheet.

Decks and images are not generated yet. That is deliberate — a mediocre generated deck is worse than no deck.

sections.title: Sending an email
sections.body:
When a task produces an **Email** and Wingman has drafted it, the task detail shows a compose block with **To**, **Subject** and the message, all editable.

Wingman fills the recipient only when the draft names a real address. If it wrote *"To: Chad"*, the field stays empty — a name is not an address, and guessing is how mail reaches the wrong person.

**Send** takes two presses. The second one names the recipient so you can see exactly who it is going to. Sending is final, and Wingman never sends on its own.

Mail leaves from your verified sending domain. If the domain is not verified, the error says so rather than reporting a generic failure.

sections.title: Deciding what to buy
sections.body:
When a task produces a **Purchase**, Wingman researches options and lays them out as a comparison: what it is, what it costs, where that price came from, and which one it would pick.

**Prices are only shown as real when the row carries a source link.** Anything else is struck through and marked **UNSOURCED**, with a warning that it may be invented. Check those before relying on them.

Wingman does not buy anything. You click through and pay. That rule has not moved and will not.

sections.title: Review, refine, and approve
sections.body:
Everything Wingman drafts goes to **Needs review**. It never completes anything on its own.

Open a card to see the draft. Type a revision instruction — *"shorter, lead with the number"* — and run it again; Wingman revises what is there rather than starting over. Then approve, edit, redo with a note, or skip.

A card can require **proof** before it can be completed, and every card keeps an audit trail of what changed and when.

If a draft fails, the card says so and offers **▸ Try again** or **Take it myself**, instead of sitting silently in Backlog.

sections.title: The morning brief
sections.body:
Your brief lands by email at **6:30 in your local time**, every day. It runs from two fixed UTC firings with a local-time gate, so it stays at 6:30 across daylight saving without anyone remembering to change it.

On **Today** you can regenerate it, mail it to yourself, or turn on phone alerts.

If a scheduled brief fails to reach your inbox, Today shows a red banner with the actual reason. Silence is not treated as success.

sections.title: On your phone
sections.body:
The bottom bar holds five slots: **Today · Needs review · Missions · Wingman · ☰ More**. They are chosen by how often you need them daily, not by importance — Goals is a monthly surface and Crew is weekly, so both sit behind More along with Docs & help, Settings and your travel profile.

**Needs review** takes a slot only when it has something in it.

Add the app to your Home Screen to get push notifications.

sections.title: Your crew
sections.body:
**Crew** lists everyone work is assigned to. Add real members in **Settings → Crew members**; that creates their sign-in and can send them a welcome email.

A name typed onto a card is not the same as a member. Anyone without an account is marked **NO ACCOUNT** on Today's workload, because work assigned to them is tracked here but they cannot sign in, cannot see it, and will never be notified. Add them properly and that goes away.

Members can be scoped to one workspace and to only the tasks assigned to them.

sections.title: Asking Wingman about the app
sections.body:
**Docs & help** has an Ask box. Ask it how something works and it answers from these pages, keeping the earlier turns as context so follow-ups make sense.

The conversation follows you between devices in real time — ask on your laptop and it appears on your phone. If you are signed out it says *this device only* rather than pretending to sync.

**Clear conversation** really deletes it.

sections.title: How Wingman decides
sections.body:
Wingman assembles each draft from four things: the task itself, the matching **skill**, anything in its **memory** that applies, and any context you attached.

Its hub has three tabs: **Queue** (what it is working on), **Memory** (what it knows about you and how you work), and **Plays** (repeatable routines like the weekly review or a demo follow-up).

Memory is what makes the second draft better than the first. Correcting a draft is worth more than re-writing it yourself.

sections.title: Activity recording and your grade
sections.body:
The app records what actually happens — tasks created, work routed to Wingman, drafts finished, drafts reviewed, files produced, emails sent. Your AI usage grade is computed from those records.

**Settings → Activity recording** states plainly whether recording is working, how many events this session, and the last error if there was one. If it says nothing is being recorded, the grade has nothing to read and you should say so rather than trusting a number.

Nobody but your workspace admins can read these records, and they cannot be edited or deleted once written.

sections.title: Where your data lives
sections.body:
Everything lives in your own Supabase project: tasks and workspace data, the activity log, your Ask conversation, and any files Wingman produces.

Access is enforced at the database, not in the browser. Your Ask conversation is scoped to you alone — a workspace admin cannot read it.

Email goes out through Resend from your verified sending domain.

sections.title: Admin reference
sections.body:
**Sending domain** — verify it at resend.com/domains, add the DNS records it lists, then set `RESEND_FROM` in Vercel to an address on that domain and redeploy. Until both are done, no mail is delivered.

**Scheduled brief** — two daily crons at fixed UTC hours; `api/brief.js` lets exactly one through at 06:30 local. Knobs: `CRON_LOCAL_HHMM`, `CRON_LOCAL_TZ`, `CRON_SKIP_LOCAL_GATE`.

**Keys** — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for drafting, `RESEND_API_KEY` and `RESEND_FROM` for mail, `CRON_SECRET` for the schedule, `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` for push.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.body:
**A draft never arrived.** The card says why. If Wingman stalled it offers Try again; if there is no API key it says that instead.

**The brief did not reach my inbox.** Today shows the real error. Almost always the sending domain is unverified or `RESEND_FROM` is unset.

**A teammate cannot see anything.** Check whether they have an account — Today marks people with none. A name on a card is not a login.

**Nothing is being recorded.** Settings → Activity recording tells you, including the last error.

**A task will not draft.** If it produces something but has no definition of done, it is parked in Waiting on you. Say what done looks like.
